channel.title: XKSH808 - Notes from the Shop
channel.description: Plain talk about getting found online, from Honolulu. Short posts, no jargon.

item.title: The Button That Goes Nowhere.
item.description: Somebody clicks "Book Now" on your site. Nothing happens. Not an error page. Nothing. The button just sits there. Here's why. That button points at a page. Somebody renamed the page, or deleted it, or moved the menu. The button still points at the old spot. It's been pointing at nothing for a year.

item.title: The Airplane on Your Screen Isn't About Flying
item.description: My mother called me from a restaurant. "My phone says No Service." I asked if she was holding it. She was. Then I asked the question that fixes it half the time. Is there a little airplane at the top of your screen? Silence. "There is." The airplane is airplane mode. It cuts the phone off from the

item.title: You Don't Hand Over the Whole Keychain.
item.description: When you hire somebody, you give them a key. Not the safe combination. Not the bank login. One key, one door, the hours they work. Automation should work the same way. Most of it doesn't. Most tools want everything. Your email. Your calendar. Your whole account. All of it or none of it. So people ei

item.title: You Have the Ramp. Nobody Told Google.
item.description: There's a row of little labels under your shop's name on Google. "Wheelchair accessible entrance." "Free parking." Somebody filters for a ramp. You disappear. Not because you don't have one. Because nobody ever told Google you do.

item.title: You Can't Get Into Your Own Website.
item.description: The phone number on your site is wrong. Has been for a while. You want to fix it. You go to fix it. And you can't. You don't have the login. The person who built the site has it. The nephew. The agency. The guy who was going to do your SEO. Whoever it was, they're not answering anymore. So the wrong

item.title: Stop Typing. Tap the Little Microphone.
item.description: My aunt types with one finger. It took her four minutes to write "see you at five." The keyboard is the smallest thing on the phone. Twelve letters under a thumb, and every one of them the wrong one. Then autocorrect turns it into a word she never said, and she sends it anyway, because starting over

item.title: It Writes It. It Doesn't Send It.
item.description: The reply was written before I got up. It just wasn't sent. That's the part people picture wrong. They hear "automation" and see a machine out there doing things on its own. Fair. That would make me nervous too. Mine drafts. It doesn't decide. This morning there were three things waiting.

item.title: There Are Two of You on the Map. You Only Made One.
item.description: Someone types your shop name into their phone. Two cards come up. Same name. Same street. One says you close at five. The other says six. One has your old phone number on it. The other has a photo from before you repainted. You didn't make the second one. A customer made it. Or a directory.

item.title: Your Website Didn't Break. The Name Expired.
item.description: The website didn't break. The name it lives at expired. You go to send somebody the link. You type it in yourself first, just to check. And it's not your shop. It's a page of ads. "Related Searches." A button offering to sell you the name back. Nothing got hacked. Nothing got deleted. The name.

item.title: The Screen Is Stuck. Hold the Button Down.
item.description: The screen freezes. Maybe on a photo. Maybe on a text you were halfway through. Maybe on nothing at all — just a white page. You tap it. You tap harder.

item.title: You Don't Learn It. You Just Tell It.
item.description: Every piece of software I've ever bought wanted me to learn its words first. Fields. Tabs. A dropdown with forty choices, and none of them mine. I don't have the time. Neither do you.

item.title: The Picture of Your Shop Is From a Day You Were Closed
item.description: Somebody's deciding whether to drive over. They pull up your listing. There's a picture of your shop. Shutter down. Lot empty. Flat grey light.

item.title: You Don't Have a Website. You Have a Facebook Page.
item.description: Somebody hears about you. Types your name into their phone. Up comes a Facebook page. Maybe it's yours. Maybe it's one somebody made for you years ago. They tap it. And Facebook asks them to log in first.

item.title: It Went Dark While You Were Reading
item.description: You're reading something. Maybe a text from your daughter. Maybe the instructions on a bill. Halfway down the screen. Right when you get to the important part. It goes dark. You tap it. It comes back. You find your place. You keep reading.

item.title: You Closed at Six. It Didn't.
item.description: You flip the sign. Lock the door. Drive home. Dinner. Shower. Some TV. Meanwhile the day's still not finished. Somebody left a review at 8. A reminder needs sending. The follow-up you meant to write.

item.title: Your Listing Says Permanently Closed. You're Open.
item.description: Somebody looks you up. Your name comes up. And under it, in plain words: Permanently closed. You're not. You're right here. Same door, same hours. But they don't know that. They see closed, they believe it, and they move on to the next place.

item.title: The Little Circle Spins. They've Already Left.
item.description: You know the little circle. It spins while a page loads. Somebody types your name into their phone. Taps your shop. The circle starts spinning. One second. Two. They're standing on the sidewalk with somewhere to be. So they hit back. And call the next place. Your site isn't broken. It's just slow.

item.title: Your Phone Won't Charge. Look in the Little Hole.
item.description: You plug it in at night. Same cord, same spot. In the morning it's dead. So you figure the battery's gone. Or the phone's done. Time for a new one. Maybe not. Look at the little hole where the cord goes in. Pocket lint. That's usually it.

item.title: One Board. Everybody Sees the Whole Thing.
item.description: In a shop, you call the order out. Everybody hears it. Cook, counter, whoever's bagging. Nobody has to be told twice. Software doesn't usually work like that. You do your part, then you hand it to the next person. And something gets lost in the handoff.

item.title: Your Hours Are Right on the Door. They're Wrong Online.
item.description: The hand-written hours are taped to your door. You update them when they change. Holidays, early close, whatever. Somebody checks before they drive over. Not the door. The phone. And the hours they find are last year's. Closed at six. You're open till eight.

item.title: It Looks Fine on Your Laptop. It's a Mess on Their Phone.
item.description: You built your website at the kitchen table. On the laptop. It looked good. But that's not where they're looking. They're on the sidewalk. On a phone. One hand. Sun in their eyes.

item.title: The Words Are Small. You Can Make Them Bigger.
item.description: You're holding the phone out at arm's length. Trying to read the menu. It's not working. Your eyes aren't the problem. The words are just small.

item.title: It Forgets, On Purpose
item.description: Everything I need to remember goes in my notes app. Phone numbers. A half idea. What somebody told me at the counter. It just sits there. It doesn't lift a finger on its own. And that's fine — it's a notebook.

item.title: Your Listing Says You Sell Something Else
item.description: Somebody wants what you sell. They type it in. You don't come up. Not because you're missing. You're on the map. You've got reviews. Your pin's in the right spot.

item.title: Your Website Says Not Secure. Right Next to Your Name.
item.description: Somebody looks you up. Your name comes up. And right there in the address bar, in front of your shop's name, it says: Not Secure. They don't know what that means. They just know it sounds bad. So they back out and call the next place.

item.title: Your Phone Dings at 2 AM. Here's How to Stop It.
item.description: Your phone goes off at 2 in the morning. A ding. A buzz on the nightstand. You're awake now. It's almost never anything. A store you bought from once. A news alert. Somebody's group text.

item.title: Nobody Takes a Two-Hour-a-Week Job
item.description: There's a job in your shop that takes about two hours a week. You can't hire for it. Nobody wants two hours a week. And by the time you'd explain it, train them, check the work — you've spent the two hours anyway.

item.title: The Map Sends Them to the Wrong Block
item.description: Somebody's looking for you. They pull up the map and hit directions. It takes them two blocks over. A parking lot. Somebody's driveway. They look around. No shop. They give up and go somewhere else. You never hear about it.

item.title: You Changed Your Number. Your Website Didn't.
item.description: Somebody's phone breaks. Water, drop, whatever. So you get a new number. You tell your friends. You tell your regulars. You tell the guy who does your insurance. You forget the website. That number on your contact page? Still the old one.
